about: Trial of the solar-era settings on 16 Arcturus atlas pages (31 page-epochs), 2026-10-28, before refitting the whole atlas with fit_fts_batch.py --arcturus. 'old' is the committed full-coverage record (data/corrected/atlas/arcturus_atlas.h5) on the same rows. Every trial run: HITRAN H2O shifts, O2 CIA, line coupling fitted both ways, species from a per-window scan, sinc at R 115,700, AFGL 1994 profiles per epoch (kitt_peak_1994_spring_afgl / _winter_afgl). 'strength' adds the step3_iter1 line-strength table; 'cleanNNN' add the clean-pixel telluric fit at pressure-width scale N/100.
flatness_method: niratl ships the authors' own corrected solar spectrum (Wallace, Hinkle & Livingston 1993). Ours minus theirs mixes both corrections' errors, so instead each is scored on its own, the same way: at pixels where the model transmission is below 0.97 and the solar model is flat (above 0.995 of its continuum), the rms of the corrected spectrum about a running mean of nearby pixels with neither solar nor telluric absorption. A perfect correction leaves noise there. The first and last 50 pixels are not scored: an edge pixel is inside the neighbouring page too (pages overlap by 5 cm-1), and a fit that leaves edges out should not be judged on them. Nor are pixels below a transmission of 0.15, which the corrected products blank: dividing by a saturated core turns a percent of model error into a spike that can outweigh the rest of a window. Two bins: every telluric pixel (T < 0.97) and the deep ones (T < 0.7).
